FAQs

Website Repair FAQ: Common Website Repair Questions Answered

When something goes wrong with your website, you may have questions about what caused the problem, how long the repair will take, and whether your website can be fixed without rebuilding everything.

Our website repair FAQ answers common questions from business owners, website managers, agencies, and marketers dealing with broken pages, WordPress errors, layout problems, slow websites, migration issues, malware, server errors, and other technical problems.

Whether you need immediate website repair help or simply want to understand your options before starting, the answers below can help you determine the next step.

Quick Answers About Website Repair

Can my website be fixed?

In many cases, yes. A website does not necessarily need to be rebuilt just because part of it has stopped working.

Common issues that may be repaired include:

  • Broken pages or website sections
  • WordPress errors
  • Plugin and theme conflicts
  • Elementor or Divi layout problems
  • CSS and mobile display issues
  • 403, 404, and 500 errors
  • Database connection problems
  • Website issues after an update
  • Problems after website migration
  • Broken forms and contact features
  • Slow-loading pages
  • Redirect problems
  • DNS and hosting configuration issues
  • Indexing and technical SEO problems
  • Malware and hacked website issues

The first step is identifying the actual cause. Some problems have a simple fix, while others require deeper troubleshooting involving the website files, database, server, hosting environment, or third-party services.

How much does website repair cost?

Website repair cost depends on the type and complexity of the issue.

A small issue, such as a broken section, formatting problem, plugin error, or minor WordPress problem, may require less time than a database failure, hacked website, failed migration, or major server issue.

Before work begins, we review the issue and determine the likely scope of the repair. When possible, we provide a clear quote based on the problem rather than asking you to commit to unnecessary work.

How long does website repair take?

The time required depends on what is causing the problem.

Some minor issues can be diagnosed and repaired within a few hours. More complex website troubleshooting questions may involve checking multiple areas, including plugins, themes, website code, databases, server logs, DNS settings, backups, or hosting configurations.

Factors that can affect repair time include:

  • The complexity of the issue
  • Whether the website is accessible
  • The platform and technology being used
  • Access to hosting and website files
  • Availability of backups
  • Third-party plugin or service problems
  • Database or server damage
  • The need to test the repair across devices

After reviewing the issue, we can give you a better idea of the expected repair process and timeframe.

What information do you need to repair a website?

The information needed depends on the issue. For example, a broken WordPress website may require different access than a DNS or email configuration problem.

We may need access to relevant areas such as:

  • WordPress or website administrator login
  • Hosting account or hosting panel
  • Domain or DNS settings
  • FTP or file manager access
  • Database access, when necessary
  • Cloudflare or other CDN settings
  • Website backups
  • Error messages or screenshots

You should only provide access through secure and appropriate channels. If you are unsure what access is needed, we can first discuss the problem and identify the relevant information.

Can you repair a website without rebuilding it?

Yes, when the underlying issue can be isolated and repaired.

For example, a website with a broken layout after an update may only need the conflicting plugin, theme setting, CSS, or template corrected. A website with a database error may need database troubleshooting rather than a complete redesign.

However, if a website is severely outdated, heavily damaged, unsupported, or has accumulated multiple technical problems, rebuilding certain parts may sometimes be the more practical option. We focus first on understanding the issue before recommending major changes.

Website Repair Help for Common Problems

A broken website can mean many different things. One business may have a homepage that no longer loads, while another may have a mobile layout issue, database error, missing content, or website that stopped working after a plugin update.

Our website repair help covers a wide range of common technical problems.

My Website Is Showing an Error Message

Errors such as 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 500 Internal Server Error, database connection errors, or white screens can have different causes.

The repair process may involve checking:

  • Server and hosting configuration
  • Website files
  • File permissions
  • Plugins and themes
  • PHP compatibility
  • Database connections
  • Recent website changes
  • Redirect rules
  • DNS settings

The error message can provide an important starting point, but a proper diagnosis is usually needed to determine the actual cause.

My WordPress Website Is Broken

WordPress websites can experience problems after plugin updates, theme updates, PHP changes, failed installations, or conflicts between website components.

Common WordPress repair FAQ questions involve:

  • White screen issues
  • Plugin conflicts
  • Theme problems
  • Broken Elementor pages
  • Website errors after updates
  • Login problems
  • Missing website content
  • Database errors
  • Slow WordPress performance

Depending on the problem, we can troubleshoot the affected components and test the website after the repair.

My Website Layout Is Broken on Mobile

A website may look correct on a desktop computer but display incorrectly on a phone or tablet.

This can happen because of:

  • CSS conflicts
  • Responsive settings
  • Page builder issues
  • Recent updates
  • Theme changes
  • Incorrect image sizing
  • Custom code conflicts
  • Cached files

Mobile layout problems should be tested across relevant screen sizes after changes are made.

My Website Broke After an Update

A plugin, theme, WordPress core, or server update can sometimes cause compatibility issues.

If your website broke after an update, it may be possible to identify the change that triggered the problem and repair the affected functionality. In some situations, restoring a stable version or correcting a compatibility conflict may be part of the troubleshooting process.

The best approach depends on the specific website and what changed before the issue appeared.

Website Repair Questions About Specific Issues

Can You Fix a Website That Will Not Load?

Yes. A website that does not load can often be diagnosed by checking the area where the failure is occurring.

Possible causes include:

  • Hosting or server problems

  • Domain or DNS misconfiguration

  • Expired services

  • Corrupted website files

  • Database connection issues

  • PHP errors

  • Plugin or theme conflicts

  • SSL certificate problems

  • Firewall or security settings

  • Recent website changes

The first step is determining whether the problem affects the entire website or only specific pages or features. Once the cause is identified, we can recommend the appropriate repair.

Can You Fix a Hacked Website?

In many cases, yes. A hacked website may require more than simply removing suspicious files. The repair process can involve identifying malware or unauthorized changes, removing affected files, restoring clean website components, correcting vulnerabilities, and reviewing security settings.

Depending on the situation, we may also check:

  • Administrator accounts

  • Plugins and themes

  • Website files

  • Database changes

  • Redirects

  • File permissions

  • Server security settings

  • Outdated software

  • Available backups

If a website is redirecting visitors to another site, displaying suspicious content, or behaving unexpectedly, it should be investigated as soon as possible.

Can You Fix a Slow Website?

Yes. Website speed problems can have many causes, so we first identify what is contributing to the slow performance.

Common causes include:

  • Large or unoptimized images

  • Too many plugins

  • Poorly configured caching

  • Slow hosting resources

  • Heavy themes or page builders

  • Unoptimized CSS and JavaScript

  • Database issues

  • External scripts

  • Unnecessary redirects

A proper speed repair focuses on the actual bottlenecks rather than applying random optimizations that may create new problems.

Can You Fix Broken Contact Forms?

Yes. If your website form is not sending messages, displaying errors, or failing to work correctly, we can investigate the form configuration and related systems.

Possible issues may involve:

  • Form plugin errors

  • Incorrect email settings

  • SMTP configuration

  • Spam protection conflicts

  • JavaScript errors

  • Hosting restrictions

  • API connection problems

  • Plugin updates

We can test the form after repair to help confirm that submissions are working as expected.

Can You Fix Website Problems After Migration?

Yes. A website migration can sometimes result in missing files, broken links, database errors, incorrect redirects, SSL problems, or lost functionality.

Migration-related troubleshooting may include checking:

  • Website files

  • Database connections

  • Domain settings

  • DNS configuration

  • URLs and redirects

  • SSL setup

  • Missing images or content

  • Plugin and theme functionality

  • Search engine indexing concerns

If your rankings dropped after website migration, we can also review technical SEO issues that may have affected crawling, indexing, redirects, or page accessibility.

Can My Website Be Fixed if I Do Not Know What Is Wrong?

Yes. You do not need to identify the technical cause before asking for help.

Many website owners only know what they can see, such as:

  • “My website is down.”

  • “My homepage looks broken.”

  • “My Elementor page changed.”

  • “My website stopped working after an update.”

  • “My forms are not sending.”

  • “My website is redirecting somewhere else.”

  • “Google is no longer showing my pages.”

  • “My website became very slow.”

  • “My mobile version looks wrong.”

That is enough to begin. Explain what you noticed, when the problem started, and whether anything changed before the issue appeared. Screenshots or error messages can also help speed up the initial diagnosis.

What Happens During Website Troubleshooting?

Website troubleshooting usually starts by reproducing or confirming the problem. We then investigate the parts of the website most likely connected to the issue.

Depending on the problem, this may include reviewing:

Recent Changes

Updates, migrations, plugin installations, theme changes, server changes, or code modifications can provide important clues.

Website Files and Configuration

Broken or missing files, incorrect permissions, configuration errors, and corrupted settings can affect website functionality.

Plugins, Themes, and Integrations

Third-party tools can sometimes conflict with each other or become incompatible after an update.

Database and Server Connections

Some website problems originate from failed database connections, corrupted tables, limited server resources, or configuration issues.

Browser and Device Behavior

A problem may only appear on certain browsers, screen sizes, or devices. This is particularly important for responsive layout and display problems.

Testing After the Repair

After making changes, the affected pages or features should be tested to help confirm that the original problem has been resolved and that the repair has not caused another issue elsewhere.

Website Repair Cost: What Determines the Price?

There is no single answer to how much does website repair cost because every technical issue is different.

The cost can depend on:

  • Type of website and platform

  • Complexity of the issue

  • Time required for diagnosis

  • Number of affected pages or features

  • Whether the problem involves code or database repair

  • Server or hosting involvement

  • Malware or security concerns

  • Urgency of the repair

  • Whether additional testing is required

A minor formatting issue may require a very different level of work than a website crash, migration failure, or complex database problem.

Our approach is to understand the issue first and provide a clear scope before unnecessary work begins.
